blocks.arabic_text: قَالَ: يَامُعَاذُ! قَالَ: لَبَّيْكَ يَارَسُولَ اللهِ وَسَعْدَيْكَ ثَلَاثاً قَالَ: مَامِنْ أَحَدٍ يَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاٰ إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَّسُولُ اللهِ صِدْقاً مِّنْ قَلْبِهِ إِلَّا حَرَّمَهُ اللهُ عَلَي النَّارِ قَالَ: يَارَسُولَ اللهِ أَفَلَا أُخْبِرُ بِهِ النَّاسَ فَيَسْتَبْشِرُوا؟ قَالَ: إِذاً يَتَّكِلُوا وَأَخْبَرَ بِهَا مُعَاذٌ عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ تَأَثُّماً.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه البخاري، باب من خص بالعلم قوما.، رقم:١٢٨
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Anas ibn Malik narrates: “Once Rasulullah ﷺ and Hazrat Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA) were travelling on the same mount. When the Prophet ﷺ called, “O Mu'adh ibn Jabal!”, Mu'adh (RA) said, “Labbaik ya Rasulallah wa sa'daik (O Messenger of Allah, here I am, present before you).” Then he called again, “O Mu'adh!’ and he said, “Labbaik ya Rasulallah wa sa'daik.” After calling him in this way three times, the Prophet ﷺ said, “Whichever person testifies with a truthful heart that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah, Allah has made the Fire haram upon him!” Hazrat Mu'adh (RA) asked, “Shall I tell the people this (good) news? They will be overjoyed!” The Prophet ﷺ said, “They will rely on this alone (and give up doing deeds).” Out of fear that he would be guilty of the sin (of concealing a hadith), Hazrat Mu'adh (RA) narrated this hadith at the time of his death.”

blocks.text: Explanation: For ahadith such as these, which say in effect that the affirmation ‘La ilaha illallahu Muhammadur Rasulullah’ alone is enough for the Fire to be made haram, the commentators give two kinds of explanation. 1.
